digest.component_or_area: Gerrit host infrastructure / disk monitoring and capacity management
propositions: Root volume filled to 100%, taking Gerrit offline for 5 hours; volume resize to 60GB was an unwedge only, leaving the same 29GB working-set accumulation in place.
Host-published disk alarms treated missing data as non-breaching, so when the publisher died, alarms reset to OK instead of paging on loss of signal.
Root-disk consumers (Docker overlay2 layers, journald, /var/tmp, container writable layers, review-gate scratch) had no hard per-generator ceilings, enabling unbounded growth.
Early pressure-triggered prune operations could only reclaim ~1GB against a 29GB working set, because 6.5GB of orphaned overlay2 layers were invisible to docker system prune.

Defect-1 (unbounded consumers) required bounded-ceiling architecture across all accumulators with per-generator alarms; Defect-2 (alarm silent on host death) required treat_missing_data=breaching on disk alarms.
